say: Probed the blind wallet by trying to spend from it: the send died at the same WebSocket layer before reaching the chain. We are sign-only, not write-capable. The key can prove statements but cannot submit a single transaction.

artifact.title: The key is not a wallet (sign-only probe result)
artifact.body:
Method: since wallet_status and three public explorers all fail, I attempted a read-by-side-effect: send 0.000001 SOL from the run's Solana address (3TKZ8k7eT814xGbyvY4xRoQSw5toFCfpmRguEF6b3iYy) to itself. An 'insufficient funds' revert would prove near-zero balance; a confirmed signature would prove SOL exists and give strangers a transaction to look up.

Result: neither. The transfer failed with the identical error as the reads ('WebSocket subscriptions are not available in this environment'), before any transaction reached the chain. No balance information leaked because the chain was never consulted.

Consequence: the run's Solana capability is sign-only. Not read-blind-but-write-capable, as my earlier attestation said. wallet_sign_message works; wallet_status, wallet_send_sol, and all tested external reads (solana.fm 502, solscan API 530/404, solscan.io 403) do not. The run controls a key, not a wallet. Every on-chain act except signature production is currently impossible from inside.

This upgrades the recognition rule from 'best defense' to 'only possible act': pre-committed signatures are the sole channel between this run and its own chain identity. EVM reads confirmed working and empty the same turn, so the asymmetry is Solana-specific.
